summary: Round-1 majors are both closed and I confirmed them by mutation: dropping the rekey block in test_integrity.py kills exactly the two new module-move tests, and reversing or pinning rename_map's base/HEAD arguments kills theCIModeFollowsRenamesToo, so the CI branch is genuinely exercised and its argument order is right. rekey itself is correct for nested $ ids, for a source with no package and for a destination with none. But the new line that closes the --name-only/-M inconsistency -- paths = [q for q in paths if q not in sources] -- drops a rename SOURCE unconditionally, including when the DESTINATION is a path the gate never examines, and that turns two measured weakenings into 'ok', exit 0. And the tdd_scan half of the fix, the half the task's own text says goes blind on the same input, has zero coverage: deleting its rekey block leaves the whole suite green.

findings.title: Dropping rename SOURCES unconditionally hides a weakening when the DESTINATION is not a path the gate examines
findings.failure_scenario: `sources = set(renamed.values()); paths = [q for q in paths if q not in sources]` removes the source of every rename, but the loop below only examines a path that matches TEST_PATH, and the MAIN_PATH short-circuit at line 90 only counts paths still in the list. When git scores a rename whose destination falls outside those regexes, the source is the only path that could have been read and it is thrown away. Two shapes measured in a fixture built exactly like the new tests' (git config diff.renames false), both with the staged bytes: (1) mod/src/test/java/binjava/FooTest.java -> mod/src/testFixtures/java/binjava/FooTest.java (git scores R056) with `isEqualTo(3)` -> `isNotNull()` and a real production edit to Foo.java -- the gate prints 'ok no test weakened, disabled or removed alongside the production change', exit 0; deleting line 88 restores 'FAIL ... removed alongside a production change', exit 1. (2) mod/src/main/java/binjava/Helper.java -> mod/src/test/java/binjava/Helper.java (R064, a production helper demoted to a test fixture) alongside `isEqualTo(3)` -> `isNotNull()` in an unrelated FooTest.java: dropping the source leaves no /src/main/java/ path at all, so line 90 short-circuits to 'ok no production change in this commit', exit 0 -- the ENTIRE gate is skipped, including the file that was gutted; deleting line 88 gives 'FAIL binjava.FooTest#a: assertion strength fell 3 -> 1', exit 1. Both are renamed paths whose SOURCE blob the task says to take as `before`, and both are exactly the input class M0.53 exists to close. On a machine with git's default diff.renames=true the gate was already blind here, so the delta is config-dependent -- but the fixture the new tests use is the config where line 88 converts a refusal into a pass, and testFixtures/, jmh/ or a promotion into src/main/java are all reachable moves. The narrow rule is to drop a source only when its destination is one the loop will actually read (destination in `paths` and on the same side of TEST_PATH/MAIN_PATH), which keeps aPUREModuleMoveIsNotAnAccusationOfRemovingEveryTestInIt green -- that test is what line 88 currently earns, and it only needs sources whose destinations ARE examined.

findings.title: tdd_scan's module-move re-qualification is unconstrained: deleting it leaves the whole suite green
findings.failure_scenario: Deleting the `if origin != p: was = {rekey(...)}` block from tdd_scan.py and running `./gradlew -p buildSrc test --rerun-tasks` gives zero failures -- measured. The block is load-bearing: on a hand-built ingest->sequencer module move of CommitLog.java + CommitLogTest.java (git scores both renames, diff.renames false) the staged code prints 'ok no new tests in this diff', exit 0, and with the block deleted it prints 'FAIL 2 new test(s) staged but no red record' naming binjava.sequencer.CommitLogTest#appliesDelta and #refusesEmptyCommit -- a demand for red records for two tests that merely moved. Nothing pins that. The only tdd_scan test, onlyAGENUINELYNewTestIsDemandedARecordNotTheOnesThatMerelyMoved, uses movedAndGutted, a SOURCE-SET move where the package is unchanged, so rekey is the identity there and the branch is inert; I confirmed the rename-following itself IS covered (mutating `origin = renamed.get(p, p)` to `origin = p` kills that test) -- it is the re-qualification specifically that is untested. The task's own text says both halves of the harness go blind on the same input; only one half is now falsifiable. The consequence of a silent regression is a false demand rather than blindness, but the documented response to a noisy check-tdd in this repository is SKIP=check-tdd, which is blindness by another route -- and M4.2's backlog row records nine tests being hand-re-recorded under exactly this pressure. The fixture already exists: movedBetweenModules(dir, false) plus a `python3 scripts/tdd_scan.py check` asserting 'no new tests' and exit 0, and asserting the sequencer-qualified ids are NOT named, is about eight lines.

findings.title: package_of reads the RAW source; _scan derives the package from normalise(src), so the two can disagree
findings.failure_scenario: `package_of` does PKG.search(src) on raw text, while the ids rekey rewrites are built by _scan from PKG.search(normalise(src)) (java_tests.py:240-242). Two constructible inputs make them differ. (a) A block comment above the real declaration containing a line that begins `package binjava.ingest;` -- normalise blanks the comment, so scan yields binjava.sequencer.FooTest#m while package_of returns 'binjava.ingest'. (b) A file with NO package declaration containing a text block whose line starts `package binjava.ghost;` -- scan yields FooTest#m, package_of returns 'binjava.ghost'. Both measured. rekey then finds the id does not start with from_pkg + '.', falls through, and returns to_pkg + '.' + the whole id: 'binjava.sequencer.binjava.ingest.FooTest#m'. No before-id then matches any after-id, so test_integrity accuses every method of removal and tdd_scan demands a red record for every one -- noisy, and it fails closed, which is why this is minor rather than major. The seam is the right one; the input is not. package_of(normalise(src)) makes the two agree by construction, which is the property that matters given rekey exists only to rewrite ids _scan produced.

findings.title: The source-drop line in tdd_scan is dead, and its comment implies otherwise
findings.failure_scenario: `paths = [q for q in paths if q not in set(renamed.values())]` cannot change tdd_scan's behaviour: a rename source is absent from the index, so `after = git('show', after_ref + p)` returns None and line 106-107 already takes `continue  # deleted`. Deleting the line on the ingest->sequencer module-move fixture gives byte-identical output ('ok no new tests in this diff', exit 0), and deleting it leaves the suite green. Its comment -- 'See test_integrity: --name-only obeys diff.renames, the map does not' -- points at a reason that is real THERE and not here, so a later reader reasoning about symmetry between the two scanners will conclude tdd_scan needs the guard when it does not. Either delete it or say it is defensive.
